record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.original_question: An operator ideal A is called traceless if it admits no nonzero trace. Show that every norm-closed operator ideal is traceless.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Show that all norm–closed operator ideals are traceless.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces, and let $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ denote the Banach space of bounded linear operators from a Banach space $X$ to a Banach space $Y$. An operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is an assignment to each pair of Banach spaces $(X,Y)$ of a linear subspace $\mathcal{A}(X,Y) \subseteq \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ such that:
(i) every finite-rank operator belongs to $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$;
(ii) for $S \in \mathcal{L}(X_0,X)$, $T \in \mathcal{A}(X,Y)$, $R \in \mathcal{L}(Y,Y_0)$ one has $RTS \in \mathcal{A}(X_0,Y_0)$.
The ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is called norm-closed if for every pair $(X,Y)$ the component $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$ is closed in $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ with respect to the operator norm.

A trace on $\mathcal{A}$ is a family of linear functionals $\tau_X : \mathcal{A}(X,X) \to \mathbb{C}$ (one for each Banach space $X$) such that:
(a) $\tau_X(yx) = \tau_Y(xy)$ for all $x \in \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ and $y \in \mathcal{A}(Y,X)$ (with $yx \in \mathcal{A}(X,X)$ and $xy \in \mathcal{A}(Y,Y)$);
(b) $\tau_X$ extends the usual trace on finite-rank operators on $X$, i.e. $\tau_X(a \otimes x^*) = \langle x^*, a\rangle$ for all $a \in X$, $x^* \in X^*$.

The ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is called traceless if the only trace on $\mathcal{A}$ is the zero functional family (equivalently, no nonzero trace exists on $\mathcal{A}$).

Prove that every norm-closed operator ideal on the class of all Banach spaces is traceless.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of the conjecture that every norm-closed operator ideal on the class of all Banach spaces admits no nonzero trace. The problem is stated as an open question in Pietsch's recent work on traces of operator ideals, and no source verifying either a proof or a counterexample was located. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Operator Ideals with a Trace - Pietsch (1981)
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational paper by Pietsch on traces of operator ideals; does not establish that all norm-closed ideals are traceless.
status_evidence.claim: The general framework of traces on operator ideals is due to Pietsch; the specific conjecture about norm-closed ideals being traceless is not resolved there.

status_evidence.title: Operator Ideals — Pietsch
status_evidence.snippet: Standard monograph on the abstract theory of operator ideals on Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the conjecture is given in the standard reference monograph.
